items.title: Louis Armstrong Interview, 1960-08-16
items.q: At 6.45, Bash Kenneth tells about the

ctx.x: Well, uh, you know, here's something else. They, uh, I've heard, or you've heard, that American jazz is really dug over in Europe and, uh, all over the world, and it's a tremendous influence. They say that, uh, sometimes our jazz music is, uh, better than, uh, some of our diplomats. It does more good, uh.

Yeah, well, I don't talk about singing like that, because some people, uh, I think they can't look too far. I don't know, they probably don't go here as diplomats or something. You know what I mean, but, but the music from, uh, the people I run into, they go there with all good, happiness, pain, and that, that's the way that curtain rides. You know what I mean? Your boys will play with you. They feel the same way as you do. Yeah, they, uh, always tell them don't mess up their hustle. Mm-hmm. That means so much.…
